_readme: Level 2 main case: Aling Rosa Santos. All names, numbers and references are fictional design fixtures, not tax advice.
Full content key: Documentation/Level2SomethingDoesNotMatch/CONTENT.md. Edit text freely; IDs (caseId, review ids, document and line ids) are stable keys used by code and saves.

documents: the pages the existing case folder shows at the start (cover, prepared summary S1, payment note N1). Four supporting records arrive from Rosa at her stall (T04): D1 and D4 back the two summary lines, D3 is the separate paid job missing from the summary, D5 explains the borrowed deposit. D2 and D6 stay defined for old saves only and are never handed over.
review.documents[].documentName: which 'documents' entry is printed as that page of the case folder (must match exactly). Held pages follow Taxpayer Information, in this order.
review: the prepared-packet review data (CaseReviewDefinition). It is validated when the case loads: unique ids, starting pages that exist, summary income rows that add up to the printed subtotal.
No answer key, finding or stamp choice is printed on any page. potentialIssues stays empty because the case folder shows that list to the player.
Fields starting with '_' are notes and are ignored by the game.
caseTitle: Aling Rosa Santos - May 2026 Income Summary Review
caseSummary: Aling Rosa Santos runs Rosa's Laundry at Plaza Market, Stall 04. Review her prepared May summary against the notes and receipts behind it.
_requiredFields: The inherited taxpayer facts the Auditor still checks (Level 1 tools). Hints never give the answer. The income schedule, findings and stamp reason are graded by later Level 2 tickets.

requiredFields.hint: Check where the taxpayer lives and is a citizen.
requiredFields.mistakeCost: The wrong residency would put her income under the wrong rules.

requiredFields.hint: Check how the taxpayer earns a living.
requiredFields.mistakeCost: The wrong taxpayer type would send her to the wrong return and records.

requiredFields.hint: Check where the taxpayer's income comes from.
requiredFields.mistakeCost: The wrong income source would misdescribe her business income.

_documents: Printed as case-folder pages after Taxpayer Information, in page 1's font. Keep each page to 5 rows and each value short (about 20 characters) so it fits like page 1.

_clientHandover: Level 2 consistency pass: the same Client Copy flow as Marie's. After the approved Audit Summary the Auditor's hand-in conversation continues with approvalGreat / approvalGood / approvalOkay, then auditorGive, and Rosa's read-only copy drops beside him; you carry it to Rosa in the conference room, the handover line waits until you drag the copy onto her (or tap the folder icon), then explain and her clientFinale lines. afterDelivery = a tap on her afterwards. Delivery commits her follow-through once (story runs only).

review._contentStatus: educational-draft: the loan-principal teaching rule has no confirmed Philippine primary-source passage yet (see CONTENT.md, Book additions and sources). It is NOT a legal citation.
review._profileText: One sentence that lets the player work out Classification, Type and Income Source with Book Sections 1-3 without naming them: Filipino + lives here (Resident Citizen), runs her own stall with no employer (Self-Employed), paid by customers of her trade (Business Income). Level 2 consistency pass: no separate Taxpayer Profile page any more; the same facts print on the Client Background notes (background) on Supporting Documents.
review.profileText: A Filipino who has always lived in town, Rosa has no boss: she runs her own laundry stall, and customers pay her to wash their clothes.
review._background: Client Background notes (Type 2, 'Client interview notes'), the first record on Supporting Documents (page 2) from the start: profileText's facts in the fixed HOME / WORK / INCOME blocks. Never an answer label.

review._annotation: Income toolkit at the market desk (T05). typeOptions/treatmentOptions are the TYPE and TREATMENT note cards (general rules only, never Rosa-specific). tutorial is T0, an unrelated fictional payslip the guide demonstrates once and the player repeats; it is never scored. entries (Rosa's E1-E4) and their separate answer keys arrive with T06.

typeOptions.label: Compensation income
typeOptions.rule: pay from an employer for work done as an employee.

typeOptions.label: Business / service income
typeOptions.rule: money earned from your own trade or from jobs done for customers.

typeOptions.label: Rental income
typeOptions.rule: money received for letting someone use your property.

typeOptions.label: Passive income (interest)
typeOptions.rule: earnings from money or investments, such as bank interest. Check its own rule before deciding its treatment.

typeOptions.label: Borrowed funds
typeOptions.rule: money that must be paid back. Borrowing is not earning.

treatmentOptions.label: Regular income schedule
treatmentOptions.rule: earned income listed with the other income for the period.

treatmentOptions.label: Separate rule
treatmentOptions.rule: some income follows its own rule instead of the regular schedule. Check that rule first.

treatmentOptions.label: Statutory exclusion
treatmentOptions.rule: only for items a law itself excludes. Use it only when a rule says so.

treatmentOptions.label: Not income
treatmentOptions.rule: money that was not earned, such as a loan that must be repaid.

evidenceOptions.label: Payslip PS-0430
evidenceOptions.rule: the record of this pay: who paid, for what work, and when.

evidenceOptions.label: Company ID card
evidenceOptions.rule: shows where someone works, not what they were paid.

evidenceOptions.label: Bank passbook page
evidenceOptions.rule: shows money arriving, not why it was paid.

review._annotationKey: Answer key for Mark the Money! (T06): one per entry, separate from the player-facing records. Hints go from a general rule to a specific one on later checks; they never mention summary totals, findings or the stamp.

typeHints: Customers pay Rosa for washing their clothes: money from her own trade.
Payments for her laundry work are Business / service income.
treatmentHints: Money earned from ordinary work goes with the other income of the period.
evidenceHints: Which one record lists these clothes-washing payments for the month?
Clip only the monthly collection sheet, D1.
highlightHints: Find the row that states how much customers paid for clothes washing.
Highlight the Paid in May row.

typeHints: A guesthouse paid Rosa to do a washing job for them.
A paid job done for a customer is Business / service income.
treatmentHints: A paid job is earned money, like her other work.
evidenceHints: Which record was written for this job?
highlightHints: Find the amount paid for the washing job.
Highlight the row that says what was paid.

typeHints: She was paid for letting someone use her machine.
Letting someone use your property earns Rental income.
treatmentHints: This is an ordinary rental with no special rule of its own.
evidenceHints: Which receipt shows the machine being rented?
highlightHints: Find the row showing how much Rosa received for letting someone use the machine.

typeHints: Rosa has to pay this money back.
Money that must be repaid is Borrowed funds.
treatmentHints: Use Not income: it is not an exclusion, it was never earned.
evidenceHints: The bank only shows money arriving. Which record says why it arrived?
highlightHints: A bank credit shows money arriving, but check the description before treating it as income.
Highlight the credit row so you can compare it with the loan record.

review._office: Office reconciliation: the Reviewed Schedule has two lines for the summary's listed entries plus one missing entry (scheduleSlotLabels, worded so they never name the work). Values come only from the highlighted lines of the four annotated papers (scheduleSources with entryId); moneyIds stop the same payment being counted twice. F1 is the conclusion beneath the totals. officeRule is answer data for the Auditor and is never printed.
review._finalAndAudit: T08 uses a generated summary of the player-entered schedule and F1 source/conclusion, stamped as a recommendation for the Auditor. T09 audit lines per outcome and root cause point to the record or rule, never fix it. T10 review cutoff clock (active seconds per day, warnings, one late consequence).

approved: Approved. Every earned payment has a supported place, and the loan stays out.
audit.justifiedHold: You have a reason to hold this. Use the collected records to finish the unresolved item.
audit.prematureApproval: This isn't ready yet. Look at this, and at Section 9 of your book, before you approve it again.
audit.falseHold: Everything in this review is supported. Check your annotated papers before holding it again.
audit.reasonError: Your recommendation and its reason don't match what this review shows. Check the reason you chose.
audit.unchanged: Nothing has changed since I last looked. Change the review, stamp it again, then bring it back.
audit.rosaHold: Rosa: "Can this still be finished today? Tell me what you need."
audit.rosaPremature: Rosa: "I thought it was finished. Please tell me what still needs fixing."
audit.rosaFalseHold: Rosa: "I brought all my papers already. Can we use them to finish this?"

feedback.line: The missing entry still has no supported payment. Check the annotated paper for the separate blanket-washing job.
A listed line of the summary is missing from your schedule. Check each annotated paper's highlighted amount.
Money that must be repaid is not earnings. Check the loan agreement and Sections 4 and 5 of your book before counting it.
One payment is counted twice. Each payment gets one line: see Section 6 in your book.
Your conclusion below the totals should say what you did with the missing entry. Section 8 of your book lists the conclusions.
One of Rosa's taxpayer facts on the first page needs another look. Read her Taxpayer Profile again beside Sections 1 to 3.
